chapter: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
title: Nazarro tells the girl's suitor she is unworthy
summary: Bubbles sends the girl's future husband to Nazarro, who maligns her; Bubbles then says at the bar that he could not marry a white girl.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You must remind yourself sometimes of Nazarro's prejudiced. He's been that way all along but he never told about it. You can read that all over his actions.
And when I had him meet me in Nazarro's office to let him find out from Nazarro about this girl he wants me to tell him about.
Was this particular fellow black or white?
White. When Nazarro got through with him, I guess he could go through the floor-board, 'cause Nazarro called her everything but a child of God because he was marrying her

'cause she was like a negro. But this fella doesn't know that's why he's describing this girl that he is, he doesn't know that's why Nazarro is doing that. He just thinks that's just a natural way for him to be describing this girl. But I know why he's describing her like that. She ain't nothin' like he said in my book. She's just too fine and don't like him. And he thinks she should like him other than liking me. You don't like me 'cause I'm as good as this guy is. She like me 'cause I have much more to offer than this guy, especially as a human being. He may have some money, but money didn't excite her.

So anyway, he gets the information. Now I take him down to the bar and I says to the man, done told him what she is, everything, -- a child of God that she's so-and-so-and-so. In the meantime he's using an incident where the girls of this same show had given a party and no men were allowed but Buck and Bubbles with these 18 girls and he used that

term, too, to be part of her being not as good as this guy is supposed to think she is. So I take him down to the bar to have a drink or so and I just told the fella at the bar, I said, 'You know if I had the money ain't nobody would get that girl. Because she's too good for anybody I know. I depend on the white people for my livin' and I know they don't want me to have no white girl and that's why I won't marry her, that's exactly why,' I'm telling him. My mother's told me also about it. So I'm letting him know that's why we're not married and that's why we're not as close as we would have been because I can't get too close because if I get too close I'm going to get hurt in my profession. They're not going to give me no bookings, I know that. I saw that happen. So I know it backwards.
